brief: Commodities are rallying broadly, not just oil: since the start of August, European gas is up 34% and gasoline 22%, while zinc, copper, silver, platinum, gold, sugar, cocoa and corn also rise; only a handful of futures commodities (hogs, cattle, nickel, orange juice) are down over the period. Drivers cited: Iran-war damage to refinery capacity elevating diesel and gasoline and transport costs, Russia-Ukraine escalation in the Black Sea pressuring softs, a potentially potent El Nino, and a more geopolitically fractured world driving stockpiling and self-sufficiency. The Bloomberg Commodity Index is near 15-year highs, and 10-year annualized commodity returns have only been exceeded once (2008) since the 1970s commodity boom. Historically, stocks falter when commodity prices are this high (1970s, early 2010s) and do best when commodities are historically low, making today's simultaneous high stock and commodity returns an anomaly. The author argues that if commodity prices stay elevated, equities have more downside ahead, because energy-driven earnings gains will not offset broader commodity-driven inflation hurting the rest of the economy.
